nonObvious.text: A loyal customer base cannot replace the owner’s physical capacity.
nonObvious.why: Cooking, serving and ownership may all depend on the same person.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: Winning a payment does not preserve a cafe’s location.
nonObvious.why: A settlement can compensate a tenant while ending the operating lease.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A long line on closing day does not prove the prior operation could pay its obligations.
nonObvious.why: A farewell sales surge is not a normal-month revenue baseline.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A successful brand can close one unviable address while keeping another.
nonObvious.why: Location-specific demand must be separated from brand reputation.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A full queue can coexist with insolvency.
nonObvious.why: Revenue is not cash available after financing commitments.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A closed storefront can mean relocation rather than business death.
nonObvious.why: Closure datasets need outcome and legal-entity distinctions.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: Owning the building does not solve operator fatigue.
nonObvious.why: A financially valuable property and an exhausting operating job are different assets.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A bakery’s recipes do not by themselves transfer its production skill.
nonObvious.why: Retirement requires a people-and-process handover, not just a sale of ovens.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: Adding wine does not automatically make a coffee shop’s economics work.
nonObvious.why: The owner still needs contribution sufficient for the particular premises.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A cafe can close to walk-in trade while catering survives.
nonObvious.why: The relevant unit of failure may be a sales channel, not the whole company.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A health closure order and permanent business closure are not identical.
nonObvious.why: The owner can separately decide whether to fund correction and reopen.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A cafe can finish opening and still lose its entire operating runway to building repairs.
nonObvious.why: Opening permits do not ensure continued utility availability.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A matcha brand may remain alive after its last cafe closes.
nonObvious.why: Retail distribution and hospitality can have different economics.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A full calendar of community activities does not automatically pay storefront rent.
nonObvious.why: Programming popularity and cash contribution require separate measurement.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

nonObvious.text: A reopened cafe name can conceal a change of owner and business obligations.
nonObvious.why: Use legal operator identity, not just signage, when tracking survival.
nonObvious.note: Qualitative lesson inferred from this reported case; not a prevalence estimate or proof that all cafes behave this way.

failureStories.what: The neighborhood breakfast and lunch cafe stopped serving.
failureStories.cause: The owner said worsening arthritis meant prioritizing her health.
failureStories.lesson: A cafe dependent on the owner’s physical work needs an exit or replacement plan.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Owner Yoko Kubo, quoted by Greenpointers

failureStories.what: Cafe Lalo did not return to its long-time premises.
failureStories.cause: The report describes a settlement after competing claims over unpaid rent and unrepaired water damage; it does not establish either allegation as the sole cause.
failureStories.lesson: A premises dispute can end in lease surrender even when the tenant obtains money.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: West Side Rag reporting on court documents

failureStories.what: The original bakery closed its premises after a final service.
failureStories.cause: Owners previously said they would not fight refusal to extend the lease; the landlord also alleged rent arrears.
failureStories.lesson: Treat lease renewal and operating popularity as separate questions.
failureStories.quote: hours before the bakery closed for good

failureStories.what: The diner closed and the premises were seized.
failureStories.cause: Eater reports an eviction and alleged unpaid rent; succession and health-inspection issues also appear, without a single proven causal decomposition.
failureStories.lesson: Keep rent arrears and succession obligations visible before transfer of control.

failureStories.what: The Lexington Avenue coffee shop closed while the wider company remained active.
failureStories.cause: The business said its lease ended.
failureStories.lesson: A branch closure is not evidence of the whole brand failing.
failureStories.quote: our lease has come to an end
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Joe Coffee statement quoted by Eater

failureStories.what: Milu closed its Brooklyn branch while Flatiron remained open.
failureStories.cause: Connie Chung told Eater that demand never picked up enough to sustain it.
failureStories.lesson: Prove demand at the new address rather than transplanting the flagship forecast.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Owner Connie Chung, quoted by Eater

failureStories.what: The new coffee shop closed soon after opening.
failureStories.cause: A spokesperson confirmed that business failed to pick up.
failureStories.lesson: Set a launch runway and a measured demand review instead of assuming opening creates regulars.
failureStories.quote: after business failed to pick up
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Eater reporting a cafe spokesperson’s confirmation

failureStories.what: The cafe permanently closed after eviction.
failureStories.cause: Eater, citing Brownstoner, reports unpaid rent and the landlord taking possession.
failureStories.lesson: Rent paid only in part can accumulate into loss of possession.

failureStories.what: The bakery and cafe closed.
failureStories.cause: The owner described debt pressure; Eater reports a bank declined requested debt relief.
failureStories.lesson: A busy counter does not guarantee enough cash after financing obligations.

failureStories.what: The luncheonette closed its Canal Street premises.
failureStories.cause: The report attributes closure to a rent hike.
failureStories.lesson: Model renewal rent separately from the rent paid during a successful operating history.

failureStories.what: The cafe closed after its lease ended.
failureStories.cause: The cafe said its lease would not be renewed.
failureStories.lesson: Plan for a landlord’s refusal to renew even without an alleged breach.

failureStories.what: Doma closed its Perry Street premises with plans to move.
failureStories.cause: Eater inferred a landlord/rent issue from the owners’ statement; the exact terms were not established.
failureStories.lesson: Do not code a reported relocation as liquidation, or an inferred reason as proven.

failureStories.what: The cafe ended service.
failureStories.cause: Eater says the building-owning proprietor was reportedly tired of operating; this is attributed reporting rather than a financial finding.
failureStories.lesson: Owning real estate removes renewal risk but not the owner’s desire to stop.
failureStories.quote: reportedly tired of running a restaurant

failureStories.what: The daytime sandwich shop closed.
failureStories.cause: Caroline Fidanza’s announcement pointed to personal reasons, explicitly contrasting them with rent.
failureStories.lesson: Do not automatically assign rent as the cause of every beloved shop closing.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Owner Caroline Fidanza’s hashtag quoted by Eater

failureStories.what: The family bakery closed following the owners’ retirement decision.
failureStories.cause: The family publicly chose retirement after long working hours.
failureStories.lesson: Plan a successor before the founder’s intended retirement date.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: amNewYork reporting; years are historical quotation, not a model input

failureStories.what: The bakery ceased operating.
failureStories.cause: Owner Zohar Zohar told Eater she was closing for personal reasons; specific financial causes were not supplied.
failureStories.lesson: Preserve an unknown cause rather than fabricating a cost explanation.
failureStories.quote: closing the bakery for personal reasons
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Eater reporting its interview with Zohar Zohar

failureStories.what: The Avenue A cafe closed while its Lower East Side location continued.
failureStories.cause: The owner’s statement says the location became too expensive to sustain with coffee and wine.
failureStories.lesson: Test contribution from the permitted menu against occupancy cost.
failureStories.quote: too expensive to stay open any longer
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Ownership statement reproduced by EV Grieve

failureStories.what: The family stopped regular cafe service and kept its catering business.
failureStories.cause: Its farewell statement described the retail small-business model as nearly impossible to sustain.
failureStories.lesson: Closing a dining room can be a channel pivot rather than the end of the company.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Miceli family statement reproduced by EV Grieve

failureStories.what: The original bagel shop closed after a health shutdown and did not reopen under that operator.
failureStories.cause: DOHMH said pest and contamination conditions required closure; employees reported the proprietor then chose not to reopen.
failureStories.lesson: Separate the required temporary remediation from the owner’s later permanent-exit choice.
failureStories.quote: posing an imminent public health hazard
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Health Department statement quoted by ABC7

failureStories.what: The cafe opened, shut after a gas leak, and never resumed service.
failureStories.cause: Owners Colin Vickery and Leah Blewett blamed ongoing building repairs.
failureStories.lesson: Completion of the first opening does not remove building-system reopening dependencies.

failureStories.what: The long-running coffee and sandwich shop closed.
failureStories.cause: Owner Jim Montemarano described a difficult decision; the article does not establish financial downturn as the cause.
failureStories.lesson: Historical co-occurrence with a downturn is not causal proof.
failureStories.quote: an emotional quarantine deciding Cranberry’s future
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Owner Jim Montemarano quoted by Eater

failureStories.what: The family-run dog-themed cafe closed.
failureStories.cause: Completed closure is reported; no specific cause is established by this evidence excerpt.
failureStories.lesson: A themed concept requires its own cost and customer evidence; do not assign a cause from theme alone.
failureStories.quote: Black Lab Cafe closed on Monday

failureStories.what: Chalait closed its final physical cafe.
failureStories.cause: The article does not state a detailed financial cause; it describes continuation online.
failureStories.lesson: Distinguish closure of physical distribution from product-brand shutdown.
failureStories.quote: quietly closed its Upper West Side café

failureStories.what: The Upper West Side cafe closed while other branches remained.
failureStories.cause: Eater reports a rent increase; local reporting says the company sought relocation.
failureStories.lesson: Do not assume a new branch enjoys a long stable occupancy-cost period.

failureStories.what: The cafe ended service at its Amsterdam Avenue address.
failureStories.cause: The owner reportedly could no longer afford the rent.
failureStories.lesson: A prior relocation does not remove the next address’s lease risk.
failureStories.quote: poured out its last cup of coffee

failureStories.what: The coffee shop and community arts venue closed its storefront.
failureStories.cause: Owner Ian Ford blamed rent pressure and described a possible mobile future.
failureStories.lesson: A venue may keep its community mission by changing premises format.
failureStories.quoteAttribution: Owner Ian Ford quoted by Grime Square

failureStories.what: The original cafe closed before a later revival under customer-turned-owners.
failureStories.cause: The evidence confirms the original closure but does not establish its financial cause.
failureStories.lesson: Revival at the same address does not erase the previous operator’s exit.

sources.title: Edgar’s owner explains planned closure

sources.title: Caffeine Underground goes underground
sources.evidence: Owner Ian Ford described rent pressure and plans to become mobile.

sources.title: Senator Salazar lists completed local closures
sources.evidence: Press release retrospectively lists Caffeine Underground among closed businesses.
